front.title: An Architecture for Agent Coordination in Computing-Aware Optical Networks

author.organization: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

abstract.t: Computing-aware optical networks coordinate optical connectivity with the capabilities, availability, and performance of computing services. This document describes an informational architecture for coordination among joint control, transport control, network element, and compute resource agents. These roles relate local observations to domain abstractions, assess connection-and-site candidates against a common service objective, and evaluate the combined service outcome. Computing resources may be located at edge, regional, or centralized sites. Coordination supports access to existing service instances and, where authorized, new workload placement or optical resource allocation. Resource managers retain admission and execution authority. The architecture is independent of optical switching technology and agent algorithm. An Optical Transport Network (OTN) and edge computing provide a detailed realization example; reinforcement learning is an optional policy use case. This document defines no new protocol, YANG module, or optical signal format.
